                "headline": "Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 19 at 2:10PM EDT until September 19 at 2:45PM EDT by NWS Morristown TN",
                "description": "At 210 PM EDT/110 PM CDT/, a severe thunderstorm was located over\nWalden, or 7 miles north of Chattanooga, moving southeast at 10 mph.\n\nHAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to\nroofs, siding, and trees.\n\nLocations impacted include...\nChattanooga, Soddy-Daisy, Signal Mountain, Rossville, Walden,\nLakesite, Ridgeside, Fairmount, Harrison, and Red Bank.\n\nThis includes Interstate 75 in Tennessee between mile markers 1 and\n14.",

Lightning is one of nature's leading\nkillers. This  will cause arroyo and small stream flooding.\nBetween 0.75 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen.\n- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are expected over\nthe area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nGrants, Milan, McCartys, San Fidel, Skyline-Ganipa, Cubero,\nAcomita Lake, San Rafael in Cibola County, North Acomita Village\nand Acomita.\n- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

                "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by moderate to heavy rainfall is\npossible, especially in terrain and poor drainage areas.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of central, north central, and northwest Wyoming,\nincluding the following areas, in central Wyoming, Owl Creek and\nBridger Mountains. In north central Wyoming, Bighorn Mountains\nSoutheast, Bighorn Mountains West, Northeast Johnson County and\nSoutheast Johnson County.                 "headline": "Flood Warning issued September 19 at 8:57AM CDT until September 21 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Little Rock AR",
                "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in\nArkansas...\n\nCache River Near Patterson affecting Woodruff and Jackson Counties.\n\nFor the Cache River...including Patterson...Minor flooding is\nforecast.\n\n* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.\n\n* WHERE...Cache River near Patterson.\n\n* WHEN...Until Sunday night.\n\n* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Low swampy timberland along the river begins\nto flood. Flood gates should be closed and equipment moved out of\nthe low grounds along the river and tributaries.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 8:15 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 9.0 feet.\n- Bankfull stage is 9.0 feet.\n- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending\nat 8:15 AM CDT Saturday was 9.1 feet.\n- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage on\nSunday and continue falling to 7.4 feet Thursday morning.\n- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.\n- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 9.1\nfeet on 07/23/2023.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",
                "instruction": "Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars\nthrough flooded areas.\n\nCaution is urged when walking near riverbanks.\n\nBe especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the\ndangers of flooding.\n\nRiver forecasts are based on current conditions and rainfall\nforecasted to occur over the next 24 hours. During periods of\nflooding...Evening forecasts are reissued with updated rainfall\nforecasts.\n\nObserved and forecasted stage data plots are available on our\nAdvanced Hydrologic Prediction Service web page at...\nwww.weather.gov/lzk\n\nUnder the Current Conditions section...Select River and Lakes AHPS.\n\nThe next statement will be issued this evening at 900 PM CDT.",

                "headline": "Flood Warning issued September 19 at 9:50AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL",
                "description": "...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...\n\nWithlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Levy, Marion and Citrus\nCounties.\n\n.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon has been steadily rising since\nJuly, and on September 15 reached flood stage. The cause of the high\nwater along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive\nhydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a\n4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.                 "headline": "Flood Advisory issued September 19 at 4:22AM AKDT until September 20 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK",
                "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.\n\n* WHERE...Chena River Basin from Moose Creek Dam to the end of Chena\nHot Springs Road.\n\n* WHEN...Until 1000 PM AKDT Sunday.\n\n* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas. Some\nlow-water crossings may become impassable. River and stream flows\nremain elevated. Ponding of water in areas is occurring or is\nimminent.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 412 AM AKDT, gage reports indicated widespread moderate to\nheavy rain across the Chena River Basin over the past several\ndays. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain has fallen this week.\n\n- High water levels will continue to work through the Fairbanks,\nBadger, and North Pole region along the Chena and Little Chena\nRivers. Use extra caution on and along the rivers as water levels\ncontinue to run at near record to record levels for this time of\nyear. The Chena River near Two Rivers is dropping but remains\nbankfull. The Chena River below Hunts Creek is dropping but\nremains bankfull. The Chena River below Moose Creek Dam is\ncresting. The Chena River at Fairbanks will be cresting Saturday\nafternoon. We are expecting rivers to remain high through the\nweekend but gradually drop towards more normal levels through the\nweek.\n\n- For Chena River below Hunts Creek near Two Rivers :\nAt 4:00am the stage was 15.7 feet.\nFlood Stage is 17.2 feet.\nForecast: A crest around 15.3 feet is expected at 10:00am\nSaturday.\n\n\nFor Chena River below Moose Creek dam:\nAt 4:00am the stage was 24.8 feet.\nFlood Stage is 24.5 feet.\nForecast: A crest around 24.8 feet is expected at 10:00am\nSaturday.\n\n\nFor Chena River near Two Rivers:\nAt 3:00am the stage was 19.4 feet.\nFlood Stage is 19.5 feet.\nForecast: A crest around 19.1 feet is expected at 10:00am\nSaturday.\n\n\n- Http://www.weather.gov/aprfc",

                "headline": "Hydrologic Outlook issued September 18 at 4:14PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK",
                "description": "ESFAFC\n\nHigh water in the Kuskokwim River region will continue over the next\nfew days. Conditions are expected to become favorable for water\nlevels to gradually recede over the weekend and into the middle of\nnext week.\n\nLocations:\n\n* Communities across the lower Kuskokwim River and its tributaries,\nincluding, but not limited to: Kwethluk, Bethel, Oscarville,\nNapaskiak, Napkiak, Kasigluk, Nunapitchuk, and Atmauluak.\n\nHydrologic Concerns:\n\n* High water in the Kuskokwim and other area rivers (e.g. Kwethluk\nRiver, Johnson River, etc) may inundate low-lying areas in the\naforementioned communities, nearby fish camps, and other lowlands.\n\nDetails/Analysis [What's causing this?]:\n\n* Rainfall: The Kuskokwim River basin, from the mouth at Kuskokwim\nBay upstream to the headwaters in the Alaska Range and Kilbuck\nMountains, has received approximately 150 to 200 percent of normal\nrainfall this summer (June to August). These rains have continued\ninto September, with nearly the entire basin near or exceeding 200\npercent of rainfall, with much of that rainfall occurring over the\nlast few days.\n\n* Persistent High Water: This heavy rainfall has resulted in\nanomalously high water levels being routed down from the Upper\nKuskokwim to the Lower Kuskokwim. The river gages at McGrath and\nCrooked Creek are near or exceeding record levels for this time of\nyear. The water levels at these stations have crested in the last\nweek, suggesting that the water inflow to the lower Kuskokwim\nCommunities may be on the decrease soon.\n\n* Compounding Factors: In addition to the recent rainfall and\nelevated river levels, strong coastal winds brought several feet of\nsurge to the coast, causing elevated water levels near the mouth of\nthe Kuskokwim River. This effectively reduces the slope of the\nriver, slowing drainage and resulting in water becoming backed up.\n\n* Forecast Thoughts: A shift in the weather pattern will bring\nconditions favorable for water levels to decrease. Northerly winds\nwill increase Saturday and continue into early next week to 20 to\n30 kt, with higher gusts possible at times, and bring cooler and\ndrier air to the region. Precipitation will be sparse and generally\nlight. Additionally, tidal models indicate a slight negative surge\nalong the coast due to the multi-day period of strong northerly\nwinds, potentially assisting drainage of water from the lower\nKuskokwim River.\n\nLook Ahead:\n\n* After a period of weather conditions favorable for receding water,\nconfidence is growing that another strong Bering Sea storm will\naffect western Alaska late next week (Sept 23-26). A return to\nsoutherly winds and higher coastal water in conjunction to heavy\nrainfall may exacerbate river conditions once again, particularly\non the smaller tributaries such as the Kwethluk and Johnson Rivers.\nHowever, details remain uncertain at this time as confidence is low\nin storm track and intensity. Fortunately, natural tidal cycles in\nBethel and the rest of the lower Kuskokwim favor lower tides than\nusual for this timeframe which may offset any additional water or\nsurge.",
